description: The hand-verified expected result for the positive datadog-static-analyzer SARIF fixture, which is an unmodified captured excerpt of harness/artifacts/raw/datadog-static-analyzer.sarif. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py or harness/lib/normalize/severity.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.

fixture.excerpt_note: An unmodified captured excerpt of that artifact, in the sense AAP 0.6.2 requires: whole records selected, the enclosing structure preserved, and no field value edited. The 7 results are the raw artifact's own result objects at indexes 0, 609, 620, 1028, 1090, 6224 and 6799 of its 6832, retained in raw document order and complete down to their fixes, partialFingerprints, properties and region snippets -- including the ruleIndex each one states. tool.driver.rules therefore holds the artifact's COMPLETE 1093-entry rules array, byte-identical and in raw order: every result here carries an absolute ruleIndex into that array, so retaining a subset would have forced a renumbering of the very field a capture must not touch. runs[0].artifacts holds the complete 568-entry array for the same reason of principle -- it is envelope structure, and a capture keeps the envelope. The top-level key set is raw's own, which for this producer is runs and version and nothing else: no $schema is present here because none is present there, and no run.originalUriBaseIds because the producer emits none. tool.driver.informationUri, name, version and properties are raw's, and no member the raw artifact lacks was introduced. Only the JSON text differs: the raw artifact is written as one compact line and this excerpt is indented for review, which is why 'byte for byte' is asserted per JSON record under a canonical serialization rather than over the file's bytes.
fixture.excerpt_verification: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_sarif_adapter.py, RawArtifactProvenanceTests -- the per-record, per-rule and per-envelope-member comparison against the raw artifact. The sha256 above is a mutation tripwire for this run, not the provenance evidence: a digest a fixture owns can only prove self-consistency.
fixture.size_note: This is the largest fixture in the tree, and the size is a consequence of provenance rather than of the records asserted on: seven results account for about 9 KB of it and the two complete arrays the envelope requires for the remainder. The alternative -- a five-rule subset with every ruleIndex renumbered into it -- is exactly the edit F3 named, and that material is preserved as a declared derived fixture instead.
fixture.selection_rationale: Selected for spread rather than for outcome: seven distinct rule identifiers over six rule-id prefixes (bash-security, java-best-practices, java-security, javascript-best-practices, javascript-code-style, python-security) and four languages, matches against five of the twelve authoritative globs, and all four SARIF level literals this producer emits, which is why 'none' appears at row 2. That literal is the reason this capture is the one that completes the SARIF level table: neither the opengrep nor the semgrep capture can carry it, because their rules state only error, warning and note. No finding is judged, ranked or compared with any other tool's by the selection or by anything below.
fixture.features_moved_out_of_this_fixture: The authored cases the pre-rebuild fixture carried -- a top-level $schema, a five-rule subset with renumbered ruleIndex values, a three-entry artifacts array, and rule metadata supplying properties.severity, properties.problem.severity, a case-differing label and the unmapped literal NOTICE -- now live in oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-datadog-static-analyzer-features.sarif, which is declared derived in its own expected file. None of the four severity cases is reachable from captured output: measured over the raw artifact, every one of its 6832 results states a level of its own and not one of its 1093 rules carries properties.severity, properties.problem.severity or a defaultConfiguration.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root_independence: Every uri in this fixture is root-relative, and the recorded path base for datadog-static-analyzer is the scan root itself, so joining onto the base and relativizing back to the root returns the uri unchanged. These rows therefore hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file. RootIndependenceTests re-runs the fixture under a temporary root to prove it rather than restate it.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the datadog-static-analyzer entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed. It records kind scan_root with an explicit base, sarif_uri_base_id_emitted null and sarif_original_uri_base_ids_emitted false.
resolution_context.uri_base_id_walk_consequence: No artifactLocation in this fixture carries a uriBaseId, so there is no base identifier to resolve and no walk to perform. paths.resolve_sarif_location takes its final branch -- the relative reference with no uriBaseId at all -- where the runner-recorded base is the only anchor there is. That branch resolves only because the metadata records an explicit base; with kind none it would be a counted unresolvable_path rejection rather than a default.
resolution_context.path_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASIS_SARIF_NO_BASE_ID. Distinct from the degenerate-base fallback basis, which is reached only where a uriBaseId was present and its walk failed -- the basis the opengrep and semgrep captures carry.
resolution_context.severity_source: Every result in this fixture states its own level, so the first of the four sources sarif.py's _severity_for consults supplies all seven rows and severity_from_level is 7. That is a property of the captured artifact: measured over its 6832 results, every one carries a level, and not one of its 1093 rules carries a defaultConfiguration, a properties.severity or a properties.problem.severity. All four literals this producer emits are present here and each maps through the SARIF level table -- error High, warning Medium, note Low, none Info -- so severity_basis_sarif_level is 7 and no row reaches the unmapped-literal disclosure.
resolution_context.rule_object_resolution: Every result carries both ruleId and ruleIndex. The identifier comes from ruleId, which outranks the index, so rule_id_from_rule_id is 7 and rule_id_from_rule_index is 0 -- and no capture of this producer can move the indexed counter, because every one of its 6832 results carries both. The ruleIndex values are nonetheless retained verbatim and are correct against the complete rules array: rule_pointer under row_derivations is the index each result states, and the id at that pointer equals the ruleId beside it. No result carries a rule reporting-descriptor reference, so the component resolves to tool.driver by SARIF's own default and no component reason is recorded.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve: null on every row. sarif.py collects identifiers from the rule's properties.cwe and properties.tags only; no rule here carries properties.cwe, and every properties.tags entry is the single token DATADOG_RULE_TYPE:STATIC_ANALYSIS, which matches neither the CWE nor the CVE pattern. The DATADOG_CATEGORY tokens on the results are not an identifier source.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry.
resolution_context.start_line: Present on every record, as an integer, in the region of the first location.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty authored keys, one path_kind_* per path kind and one severity_basis_* per severity basis.
counters_note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool -- multi_location_records, multi_valued_cwe_records, multi_valued_cve_records and non_filesystem_paths -- are all 0 for this fixture, and each zero is an observed property of the captured records rather than an omission: every result carries exactly one location, no rule carries a CWE or CVE identifier, and every path names a file inside the scanned tree. severity_from_level is 7 and severity_from_rule_default_configuration, severity_from_rule_property and severity_absent are all 0 for the reason resolution_context.severity_source records; the three later sources are exercised by fixtures/derived-datadog-static-analyzer-features.sarif and by MessageAndSeverityTests. severity_basis_unmapped_literal is 0 because 'none' is a SARIF level with a band of its own rather than an unmapped literal.

corroboration.note: All seven records this fixture excerpts also appear in the committed dataset's 9433 rows, matched on tool, rule_id, path and start_line, and every one of the twelve fields agrees with the rows below. That is corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values: each value here was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply.

rows.message: Double quote variable expansions to prevent word splitting and glob expansion
Use of insecure hashing method md5
Considering cloning this array versus storing it directly
unsafe reflection, potential injection of the class name
